title: autotune: default batching/caching profiles + quantization presets + unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add auto-tuning defaults for batching and caching, introduce quantization presets for common GPU families, and add unit-economics CLI/reporting to help ops teams quickly surface cost/latency tradeoffs. No API breaking changes.
description: Context: customers running multi-tenant hosted and Dedicated workloads frequently hit suboptimal unit economics due to conservative batching and cache defaults and lack of recommended quant profiles. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) runtime defaults/autotune for batching and KV-cache on the serving side with conservative guardrails and opt-out, 2) curated quantization presets (8-bit, 4-bit where supported) with heuristics per GPU family and model size, 3) a unit-economics tooling addition (CLI and reporting endpoints) that computes per-route token cost, latency impact, and an automation suggestion for profile/application mapping. Changes are designed to be safe by default: autotune initially emits suggestions into the admin console and can be enabled per-tenant; quant presets are non-destructive model variants and require an explicit rollout; unit-econ tooling reads telemetry and offers actionable recommendations. Implementation notes: added a lightweight autotune controller in services/runtime/autotune with a feedback loop driven by latency SLOs and throughput targets, added quant profiles under services/runtime/quant/profiles.yaml and a small adaptor in the model-registry loader to surface variants, added CLI commands in cli/uecon to run on-demand analyses and export CSV/json reports, and added dashboard docs and guidance in docs/ops/uecon.md. Testing: unit tests for profile selection and autotune heuristics, integration test for end-to-end suggestion flow, and perf canary runs showing median token cost reduction of 12% on representative workloads with no SLO degradation. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime feature-flag and tenant-level opt-in for the first two weeks, telemetry monitored via existing console dashboards; follow-ups include richer rollout automation and a/b testing harness. Related: ENG-3245 (autotune API), ENG-3290 (unit economics reporting).
